articles.title: Cury diz que 'suplicou' a Fachin para STF concluir julgamento em uma semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à Presidência também afirmou que houve algo 'dark' que ele não sabe explicar e disse que milhares de pessoas que falavam sobre seu nome deixaram de ter alcance nas redes.
articles.summary: Candidato à Presidência também afirmou que houve algo 'dark' que ele não sabe explicar e disse que milhares de pessoas que falavam sobre seu nome deixaram de ter alcance nas redes.
articles.body:
Augusto Cury concede entrevista durante visita ao Ceagesp — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Augusto Cury ( Avante ), candidato à Presidência, afirmou que "suplicou" ao ministro Edson Fachin e aos demais integrantes do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) para que o julgamento do Caso Master fosse concluído em uma semana. Segundo ele, a demora na análise prejudica o eleitor, que deveria ter acesso às informações antes da votação de 4 de outubro.

"Eu até supliquei para o doutor Fachin e para os demais membros do STF, que tem o julgamento público, televisionado e rápido, em uma semana", afirmou durante passagem de sua campanha pelo Ceagesp, neste sábado (19).

Cury disse que o pedido de vista feito pelo ministro Flávio Dino pode fazer com que o julgamento seja adiado para depois das eleições.

"Com o pedido de vista que o Flávio Dino fez, é possível colocar debaixo do tapete e levar isso para depois das eleições", declarou.

Ele também fez críticas a Lula e a Flávio Bolsonaro e afirmou que os dois grupos teriam interesse em evitar uma apuração rápida.

"E os dois grupos, o grupo Lula da Silva e o grupo de Flávio Bolsonaro, como tem vários membros envolvidos de maneira promíscua com o Banco Master, eles não têm interesse de uma apuração rápida", disse.

Cury afirmou ainda que, na avaliação dele, a situação estaria "asfixiando a democracia".

"Consequentemente, eles estão asfixiando a democracia, porque a democracia depende de informações para que você, no ato de 04/10, exerça o mais pleno direito, que é tão rápido e tão importante para mudar o país: seja votar de maneira consciente", afirmou.

'Houve algo dark', diz Cury sobre redes sociais

Ao falar sobre sua campanha nas redes sociais, Cury afirmou que teria sido alvo de uma mudança no alcance de conteúdos relacionados ao seu nome e à sua candidatura.

O candidato disse ter denunciado a Meta mundialmente e afirmou que, nas últimas duas semanas de agosto, havia sido o nome que mais ganhou seguidores no mundo. Depois, segundo ele, houve uma queda repentina na circulação de conteúdos sobre sua candidatura.

"Você sabe que eu denunciei a Meta mundialmente, dizendo que nas últimas duas semanas de agosto eu era o nome mais falado e que mais ganhou seguidores no mundo e depois houve algo insano que ninguém entende: o algoritmo cortou todas as 1000 de pessoas que falavam do meu nome e da minha candidatura", afirmou.

Na sequência, Cury classificou o episódio como "dark" e disse não saber o que teria provocado a mudança.

"Houve algo dark que nós não sabemos, o algoritmo cortou todas as 1000 de pessoas que falavam do meu nome e da minha candidatura", disse.

Ele também afirmou que os algoritmos das redes sociais não seriam submetidos aos mesmos princípios democráticos que, segundo ele, devem orientar a imprensa e a política.

"O algoritmo não tem democracia. Vocês da imprensa livre têm democracia, mas o algoritmo não tem democracia", afirmou.

Cury critica polarização entre Lula e Bolsonaro

Durante a entrevista, Cury também criticou a polarização entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro e disse que o Brasil não deveria ficar restrito à disputa entre os dois grupos.

"O Brasil não pode ser sequestrado por duas famílias. O Brasil pertence a mais de 210 milhões de brasileiros", afirmou.

O candidato disse ainda que gostaria de disputar o segundo turno com Lula e fez críticas ao atual presidente. "O pesadelo de Lula é me ter, Augusto Cury, no segundo turno", afirmou.

Em outro momento, Cury disse que Lula e Bolsonaro "amam o poder" e classificou a disputa entre os grupos como uma "guerra de egos".

"O poder pelo poder. Aliás, ele se retroalimenta. Um precisa do outro. Isso é uma vergonha", declarou.

Cury também pediu que eleitores insatisfeitos com Lula ou com Flávio Bolsonaro considerem sua candidatura

"Vocês que são de Lula da Silva, vêm para a nossa candidatura. E vocês que estão superdescontentes com o Flávio Bolsonaro e que sabem que ele perde para Lula, venham até mim", disse.

articles.title: Empresário diz que foi excluído da venda de fazenda a Alexandre Pires | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresário Renato Guimarães alega que apresentou fazenda para o cantor e depois foi excluído da venda pelos outros dois sócios. Ele entrou na Justiça pedindo anulação de um terço da venda.
articles.summary: Empresário Renato Guimarães alega que apresentou fazenda para o cantor e depois foi excluído da venda. Ele entrou na Justiça pedindo anulação de um terço da venda.
articles.body:
A compra de uma fazenda por R$ 25 milhões pelo cantor Alexandre Pires, em Dianópolis, no sudeste do Tocantins, virou alvo de uma disputa judicial entre empresários do agronegócio . O sócio Renato Junio Pinto Guimarães afirma que foi excluído da negociação e não recebeu a parte do valor que teria direito.

O caso teve um novo capítulo nesta semana, depois que defesa de Alexandre Pires pediu que o processo tramitasse em sigilo . O argumento foi de que a exposição do caso poderia afetar a intimidade do cantor e revelar informações sobre seu patrimônio.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

A Justiça, porém, negou o pedido de segredo total. Na decisão, o juiz afirmou que o interesse público e jornalístico no caso não significa, por si só, violação da intimidade.

Em nota, o escritório Moraes Advocacia Rural, que representa Renato, afirmou que a ação busca resguardar os direitos patrimoniais do cliente. Segundo a defesa, ele continua aberto ao diálogo e a um acordo entre as partes. O g1 procurou a defesa de Alexandre Pires, mas não recebeu resposta.

Como começou a sociedade entre os empresários

Fazenda Buriti, comprada pelo cantor Alexandre Pires, fica em Dianópolis (TO) — Foto: Reprodução/Google

A disputa teve origem em uma sociedade rural de fato formada em 2019 por três empresários: Renato Junio Pinto Guimarães, Gabriel Alves de Freitas e Matheus Alves de Freitas.

O grupo atuava na exploração e na gestão de quatro propriedades rurais na região de Dianópolis: as fazendas Catarina, Sempre Verde, Arara Preta e o Lote 8 da Fazenda Buriti.

Segundo Renato, ele era responsável pela gestão diária e pelas atividades agropecuárias das fazendas. Gabriel e Matheus, por outro lado, cuidavam da parte administrativa e da documentação.

Ainda de acordo com Renato, os registros formais das propriedades foram feitos em nome de Gabriel e Matheus por uma questão de organização do grupo.

Documentos assinados pelos três, como contratos de compra e venda de imóveis rurais e comprovantes de administração conjunta, foram analisados pelo juiz Rodrigo da Silva Perez Araújo, da Vara Cível de Dianópolis.

Segundo a decisão, os documentos apresentam indícios de uma relação comercial e empresarial entre os envolvidos, e não apenas de vínculo empregatício. Procurada pelo g1 , a defesa de Gabriel e Matheus não enviou resposta.

Alexandre Pires se apresenta na Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Visita de Alexandre Pires e negociação de R$ 25 milhões

O imóvel envolvido na disputa é o Lote 8 da Fazenda Buriti, com 1.866 hectares, área equivalente a cerca de 2,6 mil campos de futebol. A propriedade fica no Matopiba, região que reúne áreas agrícolas do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia.

Segundo a defesa de Renato, o empresário apresentou a propriedade a Alexandre Pires antes do fechamento do negócio. A defesa afirma que o cantor sabia que a área pertencia aos três parceiros.

Apesar disso, a venda da fazenda, por R$ 25 milhões, foi fechada diretamente entre Gabriel, Matheus e Alexandre Pires.

Renato afirma que só soube da negociação depois que ela foi concluída. Ele alega ter sido excluído do negócio e não ter recebido um terço do valor da venda.

Ação judicial e inclusão do cantor no processo

Renato acionou a Justiça do Tocantins e pediu a anulação de um terço da venda feita a Alexandre Pires. Ele também solicitou que a existência da disputa fosse registrada nas matrículas dos imóveis rurais do grupo.

Em decisão de 22 de junho de 2026, o juiz determinou a inclusão de Alexandre Pires no processo. Segundo a decisão, a medida era necessária porque uma eventual mudança na validade do contrato poderia afetar diretamente o imóvel adquirido pelo cantor.

O juiz também determinou a manutenção do registro da existência da disputa judicial na matrícula da propriedade.

Conflito entre empresários e acionamento do MPTO

Com o avanço da disputa financeira e judicial, o conflito entre os empresários também envolveu denúncias de violência. Renato anexou ao processo um boletim de ocorrência, fotos e vídeos de episódios de confusão entre as partes.

Em uma gravação feita em julho de 2026, uma caminhonete se aproxima e bate contra o portão de uma fazenda. Em seguida, dois homens descem do veículo, atravessam a cerca e entram na propriedade.

Renato também afirmou que máquinas agrícolas foram retiradas sem autorização e que 11 cabeças de gado foram soltas em direção a uma rodovia.

Gabriel e Matheus, por sua vez, afirmam no processo que as máquinas e ferramentas pertenciam exclusivamente a eles e não faziam parte da sociedade.

Diante dos relatos de agressões e de possíveis crimes, a Justiça acionou o Ministério Público do Tocantins (MPTO) em agosto de 2026 para acompanhar e apurar o caso. Uma audiência de conciliação realizada em 27 de agosto terminou sem acordo.

articles.title: ‘Me jogando na vida’: Cissa Guimarães se aventura em tirolesa em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Atriz e apresentadora está de férias no estado e compartilhou nas redes sociais o momento da aventura em um atrativo turístico da região.
articles.summary: Atriz e apresentadora está de férias no estado e compartilhou nas redes sociais o momento da aventura em um atrativo turístico da região.
articles.body:
A atriz e apresentadora Cissa Guimarães compartilhou, nesta sexta-feira (18), um vídeo em que desce de tirolesa em Bonito (MS). De férias no estado, ela aproveita a viagem para conhecer as belezas naturais da região. Veja o vídeo acima.

Na publicação, Cissa resumiu a experiência com a frase: “Me jogando na vida”.

No registro feito pelo guia André Duratti, a apresentadora aparece animada antes do salto e recebe orientações sobre o momento de entrar na água. Após a descida, ela cai na água e gargalha. No vídeo, Cissa usa equipamentos de segurança, como colete salva-vidas.

A publicação nas redes sociais mostra todo o percurso, desde a preparação até a reação da atriz após cair na água.

A viagem faz parte das férias da apresentadora pela região, conhecida pelas atrações turísticas ligadas a rios, nascentes e águas cristalinas.

A apresentadora viaja acompanhada do marido, Hildo Assis. Juntos, eles já visitaram o Buraco das Araras, em Jardim, e depois seguiram para Bodoquena, onde conheceram a Cachoeira Boca da Onça e o Buraco do Macaco.

Com 156 metros de altura, a Boca da Onça é a maior cachoeira de Mato Grosso do Sul. O nome do atrativo deve-se a uma formação rochosa na queda-d'água que lembra o rosto de uma onça.

O casal também esteve no Buraco do Macaco, uma caverna submersa na Serra da Bodoquena formada pela erosão da água. O local conta com um lago de águas cristalinas propício para mergulho.

articles.title: Renan Santos defende 'militarizar o Brasil' contra o crime organizado | G1
articles.standfirst: Antes de ir ao Litoral Norte, candidato passou por Passo Fundo, Caxias do Sul, Gramado e Porto Alegre. Ele segue agora para Santa Catarina.
articles.summary: Antes de ir ao Litoral Norte, candidato passou por Passo Fundo, Caxias do Sul, Gramado e Porto Alegre. Ele segue agora para Santa Catarina
articles.body:
Candidato à presidência pelo partido Missão, Renan Santos segue com sua caravana pelo Sul do país, em um roteiro que iniciou no Rio Grande do Sul na quinta-feira (17) . Ele passou por cinco cidades gaúchas : Passo Fundo, Caxias do Sul, Gramado, Porto Alegre e Capão da Canoa .

Neste sábado (19), Renan cumpriu agenda na cidade do Litoral Norte. Ele chegou ao município por volta das 10h, apresentou propostas.

Discursando para apoiadores, o candidato defendeu reforçar a segurança pública.

"Eu queria falar para vocês sobre como nós vamos militarizar o Brasil e juntos vamos libertar a América do Sul do crime organizado", afirmou.

Ainda sobre o tema, ele disse que seu governo investigaria "o envolvimento de toda a classe política com crime organizado".

Ao falar sobre os candidatos Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro e a polarização política, defendeu que esta é uma "eleição da desistência" .

"Ambos querem que você não tenha nenhuma esperança de nada diferente, para que você vote no seu candidato apenas com medo do adversário", disse.

E acrescentou: "Vão votar no Flávio porque não é o Lula. Vão votar no Lula porque não é o Bolsonaro."

Após o discurso, o candidato visitou o calçadão, na beira-mar, e respondeu a perguntas da imprensa.

Depois do encerramento da agenda no Rio Grande do Sul, Renan Santos segue para Santa Catarina, onde cumpre novos compromissos de campanha.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo do Paraná intensificam ações nas ruas em carreatas, caminhadas e panfletagens  | G1

articles.summary: Agendas dos candidatos ao governo do Paraná deste sábado (19) concentram esforços em proximidade com a população.
articles.body:
Palácio Iguaçu - Governo do Paraná — Foto: Natalia Filippin/G1

Os candidatos ao governo do Paraná apostam esforços no contato próximo com a população, neste sábado (19).

Requião Filho ( PDT ) cumpre agenda nas ruas no litoral do Paraná, em Paranaguá. Sandro Alex ( PSD ) passa por três cidades em carreata na região Oeste. E Sergio Moro ( PL ) encontra seguidores em caminhadas e carreatas por cinco cidades do Norte do estado.

Adriano Funileiro ( PCO ) começa o dia em panfletagem e conversa com trabalhadores perto da rodoferroviária de Curitiba . Depois, participa de ação com venda de materiais do partido na Rua XV de Novembro, no Centro. Após o almoço, às 13h, faz uma transmissão da ‘Análise Política da Semana’, com Rui Costa Pimenta, candidato do partido à presidência, no Centro Cultural Benjamin Péret (CCBP), em Curitiba.

Alexandre Salomão (Mobiliza) concentra atividades no bairro Boqueirão e Alto Boqueirão, em Curitiba, na região da Rua Francisco Derosso. O candidato faz caminhada com apoiadores, conversa com moradores e comerciantes.

Luiz França (Missão) não tem agenda de campanha para este sábado.

Samuel Mattos ( PSTU ) participa de evento de partidos em apoio ao PSTU em Curitiba, durante a tarde.

🔍A campanha eleitoral de 2026 iniciou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Desde esta data, candidatos estão autorizados a pedir votos e realizar comícios, caminhadas, debates e divulgar suas propostas em rádio, TV e internet, seguindo as regras estabelecidas pela Justiça Eleitoral.

Abaixo, confira a programação dos candidatos melhor posicionados na última pesquisa Quaest para o governo:

Pela manhã, Requião Filho (PDT) faz carreata em Paranaguá, no Litoral do estado. O ato de campanha parte da Praça Tupi, na Vila Guarani.

Sandro Alex (PSD) também faz carreata pela manhã, saind da Avenida Tancredo Neves, em Cascavel, no Oeste do estado. À tarde, encontro com apoiadores no bairro Três Lagoas, em Foz do Iguaçu. E, na sequência, na Paróquia Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro, na Comunidade Bom Pastor, no bairro Belo Horizonte, em Medianeira. À noite, o candidato participa de um congresso da União da Mocidade das Assembleias de Deus no Estado do Paraná, na Área Industrial de Medianeira.

Sergio Moro (PL) faz caminhada com apoiadores pela manhã, em Apucarana, com saída da Praça Rui Barbosa. Depois, em Arapongas, parte em caminhada da Rua Drongo, em frente à Igreja Matriz. No início da tarde, o candidato participa de um evento na Rua Sergipe, em Londrina . Também à tarde, o candidato faz carreata em Rolândia, com saída da Avenida dos Girassóis; e em Cambé, com saída da Rua Esperança. Ainda em Cambé, Moro participa de um jantar da maçonaria.

articles.summary: José Alcides Vasconcelos, ex-vice-presidente da Acese, faleceu de causas naturais e o sepultamento ocorre neste sábado no Cemitério Colina da Saudade, em Aracaju.
articles.body:
Morre em Aracaju o empresário José Alcides Vasconcelos — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Morreu de causas naturais, aos 96 anos, o empresário José Alcides Vasconcelos. A informação foi confirmada por familiares.

Segundo a família, ele faleceu em casa nesta sexta-feira. Durante a manhã deste sábado (19), o corpo foi velado e sepultado no Cemitério Colina da Saudade, em Aracaju .

José Alcides era filho do ex-vice-governador de Sergipe, Manuel Prado Vasconcelos. Ele era viúvo e deixa seis filhos, 15 netos e nove bisnetos.

O empresário atuou na Associação Comercial e Empresarial de Sergipe (Acese), onde exerceu o cargo de vice-presidente em diversas diretorias.

articles.title: Homem morto em Brumado: vítima foi baleada na frente das filhas | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso ocorreu em Brumado. Momento foi registrado por imagens de câmeras de segurança.
articles.summary: Homem morto em Brumado foi atingido por dez disparos em um posto de combustíveis; a Polícia Civil investiga a motivação do crime filmado por câmeras.
articles.body:
Um homem de 41 anos foi morto a tiros na frente das filhas, em Brumado, no sudoeste da Bahia. O caso ocorreu na sexta-feira (18) e foi registrado por imagens de câmeras de segurança ( assista acima ).

No vídeo, é possível ver que a vítima, identificada como Edesio Jesus dos Santos , estava dentro de um carro parado em um posto de combustíveis.

Em seguida, dois homens chegam em moto, param ao lado do veículo e o passageiro atira contra o homem. Ao menos 10 disparos são efetuados . Logo após, a dupla foge do local.

Vítima foi identificada como Edesio Jesus dos Santos — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

No momento do crime, uma das filhas desce do carro e corre. Ao fim dos disparos, ela volta para retirar a irmã que estava sentada no banco de trás. Um dos frentistas que estava próximo ao veículo tenta acalmar as meninas.

Guias de perícia e remoção foram expedidas. Diligências e oitivas são realizadas para esclarecer a autoria e a motivação do crime, que é investigado pela 1ª Delegacia Territorial (DT/Brumado).

articles.title: Jajangmyeon: aprenda a receita no Chef JPB | G1
articles.standfirst: Quem ensina o passo a passo da receita é a chef Haina Chin.
articles.summary: Quem ensina o passo a passo da receita é a chef Haina Chin.
articles.body:
Jajangmyeon do Chef JPB — Foto: Reprodução TV Cabo Branco.

O Chef JPB deste sábado (19) ensina o passo a passo de um prato sul-coreano: jajangmyeon .

🔎Jajangmyeon é um prato de macarrão sino-coreano coberto com um molho espesso feito de chunjang, carne de porco em cubos e vegetais. Se originou em Incheon, na Coreia, onde trabalhadores migrantes chineses trouxeram zha jiang mian de Shandong no final do século XIX.

A receita é apresentada pelo chef Haina Chin, que os ingredientes necessários e modo de preparo do prato a base de macarrão.

Para iniciar o preparo do prato, retire as sementes da abobrinha e corte-a em cubos. Faça o mesmo com a cebola, a batata inglesa e a carne de porco, procurando manter os ingredientes em pedaços de tamanho semelhante.

Em seguida, em uma panela, aqueça o óleo de gergelim e frite a carne de porco. Quando estiver selada, acrescente a abobrinha, a cebola e a batata e refogue os ingredientes.

Quando os legumes perderem o aspecto cru adicione 1 litro de água. Deixe cozinhar por aproximadamente 15 minutos, até que os ingredientes estejam macios.

Enquanto isso, coloque a farinha de soja preta em uma tigela e dissolva-a com um pouco de água. Depois, despeje a mistura na panela com a carne e os legumes. Deixe cozinhar por mais 5 minutos, ou até o molho engrossar.

Quando o molho atingir a consistência desejada, acrescente mais um pouco de óleo de gergelim, duas colheres de sopa de maisena e o macarrão.

👨🏽‍🍳 Dica da chef: o ideal é cozinhar o macarrão até ficar al dente.

Por fim, coloque a quantidade desejada de macarrão no prato e cubra com duas conchas do molho. Finalize com gergelim, lâminas de pepino e cebolinha picada. Com isso, o jajangmyeon está pronto para servir.

articles.title: Meet Yashasvi Solanki, the Haryana girl who made history as the first woman officer from India’s Army, Navy or Air Force to become President’s ADC
articles.summary: Voices of Power News: In May 2025, Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki created history by becoming the first woman officer from any of India's three armed forces, the Arm.
articles.body: In May 2025, Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki created history by becoming the first woman officer from any of India's three armed forces, the Army, Navy, or Air Force, to be appointed Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the President of India. The President is traditionally assisted by five ADCs at any given time, three from the Army and one each from the Navy and the Air Force, a role that has for decades gone almost entirely to men. Solanki was formally presented with the prestigious aiguillette on May 9, 2025, officially marking her appointment for a tenure expected to last between two and a half to three years. Speaking about the unexpected nature of the opportunity, she has said in interviews that becoming the President's ADC was never something she had specifically dreamed of or planned for, largely because it hadn't seemed within reach. Her appointment came after a rigorous selection process, including an interaction with President Droupadi Murmu herself and the necessary security clearances, followed by a period of orientation before she formally took up her duties.From district-level sports to the Naval Armament DivisionSolanki hails from Haryana, where her early life was shaped by fairly ordinary, disciplined surroundings. Before her defence career, she was known for her sporting ability, competing at the district level in both badminton and volleyball, activities that reportedly helped build the same discipline and focus she would later carry into her military service. She joined the Indian Navy in 2012 through the Short Service Commission, entering the Logistics Branch. Over the years that followed, she built a steady, well-regarded service record, eventually rising to become a technical officer in the Naval Armament Division based in Hyderabad. Officers selected for the President's ADC role typically bring at least five to seven years of strong, consistent service behind them, and Solanki's journey through logistics and technical postings gave her exactly that kind of grounded, hands-on experience within the Navy before this historic appointment.What the role actually involvesAs ADC, Solanki is now responsible for closely coordinating the President's official engagements, staying briefed on visiting dignitaries and upcoming events, and accompanying the President during state functions, investiture ceremonies, and diplomatic meetings. She has spoken about the level of preparation the role demands, noting that she and her colleagues must stay updated on who is meeting the President ahead of every engagement, since the President can ask about any of it at short notice. Her appointment reflects a broader, gradual shift already underway within the Indian Armed Forces, including the Navy's evolving policies around allowing women to command warships and take on more cross-service responsibilities. It is worth noting that Solanki's milestone did not remain unmatched for long. In July 2026, Major Navya Shekhawat of the Army Service Corps became the second woman officer overall and the first from the Indian Army to be appointed ADC to the President, an appointment that built directly on the path Solanki had opened up a little over a year earlier.A milestone that continues to inspireSolanki's rise from a district-level sportsperson in Haryana to standing beside the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan is more than a personal career milestone; it reflects a slow but real shift in how India's armed forces are opening up their most prestigious ceremonial and protocol roles to women. For young women considering a future in the defence forces, her journey offers a clear, tangible example that roles once considered firmly out of reach are steadily becoming achievable through consistent, disciplined service.

articles.title: Meet Neha Thakur: The 25-year-old from Mandi who left air hostess training to become Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver; “I drive a truck just like my father”
articles.summary: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha .
articles.body: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.The childhood connectionTrucks were a part of Neha’s childhood because her father, Rajesh Thakur, has been a truck driver for more than two decades. Neha used to travel with him a lot. In one of her Instagram vlogs, she said that her father used to drop her in the school on a truck and she was quite fascinated by the vehicle.That fascination stayed with her even after she chose a very different path.After graduation, Neha went to Chandigarh and trained as an air hostess. She worked there, but the COVID-19 pandemic happened. The aviation industry was badly hit so she returned to her hometown after losing her job. Instead of viewing that setback as the end of her career, she began looking again at something that had interested her since childhood, truck driving.Truck driving as a professionIt was not an easy decision. Neha had to learn how to handle a heavy commercial vehicle, understand gears, clutch and brakes. She joined a driving school and obtained her Heavy Motor Vehicle licence in 2023, when she was 21. Her father played an important role in her success. He supported her decision and helped her practise with the family truck, despite the criticism and scepticism surrounding a young woman choosing truck driving as a career.The early journeys were largely local. Gradually, however, Neha moved on to longer routes. Today, she drives a 16-tonne Tata truck and has been reported transporting construction material and farm produce across interstate routes. Some accounts say she covers hundreds of kilometres during her journeys.A new challengeDriving a truck through the hills is demanding for any driver. People were often surprised to see Neha behind the steering of a heavy truck. She has spoken about the criticism and doubts she encountered when she chose this profession. But the more she drove, the less she had to explain herself.Long journeys also meant irregular meals, changing weather and nights spent away from home. Driving through narrow mountain roads, fog, rain and difficult terrain requires concentration and patience. Neha's own social-media content has increasingly shown these less visible aspects of a trucker's life.When the driver's seat became a cameraNeha also started her travel vlogging journey with this. She would record her journeys and post them on social media, giving viewers a look inside a profession most people experience only from the outside. Her videos cover her daily routine, long-distance journeys and practical aspects of handling a heavy vehicle.She in one of the videos tells that soon her audience grew and she started getting brand deals. Reports published in 2026 put her YouTube following at more than 4.5 lakh, while her Instagram following has been reported at over 8 lakh.More than a truck storyNeha never intended to become an inspiration or symbol of anything. She simply returned to something she loved and enjoyed. Her story moved from a child's fascination with her father's truck, to an air-hostess course, to finally choosing to do what she loved, the steering wheel.Perhaps the most important part of Neha's story is therefore not that she chose a profession traditionally associated with men. It is that she allowed herself to change direction.For Neha Thakur, the road eventually led back to the place where the fascination had begun with a truck, a mountain road and the confidence to take the wheel herself.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: What does Trump's new order on layoffs mean? How is it going to impact H-1B Indians?
articles.summary: US News: Amid mass layoffs being announced by several companies, the Donald Trump administration came up with a new executive order that directly links layoffs.
articles.body: Amid mass layoffs being announced by several companies, the Donald Trump administration came up with a new executive order that directly links layoffs with H-1B hiring. H-1B is a visa program that allows companies to hire skilled workers from foreign countries. It is a common allegation that companies fire their workforce while continuing to hire for H-1B as that would cost them much less. In the new executive order, the government is now telling the agencies to look at an H-1B sponsoring company's layoff record when deciding whether to approve or process H-1B-related applications.What changes?Previously, an employer's layoffs were not generally a broad standalone factor considered in every H-1B case. There are already anti-displacement rules for certain H-1B-dependent employers and willful violators, but those rules are narrower.The new order directs DOL, DHS and State Department to consider whether an H-1B sponsoring employer recently laid off US workers; plans to lay off US workers; particularly where those workers are "similarly situated" to the H-1B position being sought.What does "similarly situated" mean?It essentially means US workers whose jobs are sufficiently comparable to the H-1B position — considering things such as the job duties, qualifications, experience and location. H-1B visa program is for skilled professionals but if equally skilled Americans are fired to make space for H-1B workers, this becomes a problem now.However, the new order does not yet spell out exactly how agencies will define "similarly situated" for this broader review. Implementation guidance is still expected.Does a company having layoffs automatically mean the H-1B will be denied?No. The order does not say that. It says the agencies should consider recent or planned layoffs that negatively affect similarly situated US workers. It does not say that any layoff automatically makes an employer ineligible to sponsor H-1B workers. The precise implementation and evidentiary standards remain to be established.For example, if a company lays off marketing employees but is sponsoring H-1B software engineers for positions that haven't been eliminated, the relevance of those layoffs would be different from a situation where it lays off software engineers and simultaneously seeks H-1B workers for comparable engineering positions.Why this matters for Indian H-1B workersA majority of the H-1B workers every year come from India. The new executive order will not impact individual H-1B visa workers. The scrutiny will be on the companies hiring them.The Trump administration cited figures that 800,000 to 1.3 million American employees have been fired in the tech sector from 2022 through 2026. But the tech companies are requesting for hundreds of thousands of H-1B workers."One foreign country’s foreign minister even publicly admitted that H-1B 'has become the outsourcing visa'," the order said, referring to a former Indian minister.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: More than a century after Maine’s Penobscot Nation lost control of much of its ancestral landscape, 11,297 acres have now been returned; the wider $32.5 million effort aims to return more than 30,000 acres
articles.summary: US News: A vast stretch of Maine forest has changed hands in a return more than a century in the making. On September 16, 2026, 11,297 acres surrounding the Ea.
articles.body: A vast stretch of Maine forest has changed hands in a return more than a century in the making. On September 16, 2026, 11,297 acres surrounding the East Branch of the Penobscot River were returned to the Penobscot Nation, marking the first phase of a larger effort to restore more than 30,000 acres of ancestral homeland. The Trust for Public Land, which is partnering with the Penobscot Nation on the project, said the wider effort began in 2023 with a $32.5 million fundraising goal. So far, $20.7 million has been raised, with additional funding still needed to complete the remaining phases.A first step toward returning more than 30,000 acresThe 11,297-acre transfer is part of the Wáhsehtəkʷ land-return effort, named for the East Branch of the Penobscot River. The property lies near the base of Katahdin and just south of Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument. The first phase covers an area roughly comparable in size to the city of Portland, Maine. It includes about 15 miles of cold-water streams, 865 acres of ponds and wetlands, and habitat used by species including Atlantic salmon, brook trout and moose.The project is being carried out through a partnership between the Penobscot Nation and the Trust for Public Land. The conservation organisation purchased the broader property from timber harvesters after it came onto the market more than three years ago, while working with the Nation to raise the money needed to return the land. The partnership's broader goal is to return more than 30,000 acres to the Penobscot Nation. Completing that effort will require another $12 million, according to the Trust for Public Land and Maine Public.Land with cultural and environmental importanceThe returned property is significant not only because of its size but also because of its connection to Penobscot culture and the East Branch of the Penobscot River. The Nation plans to take an active role in caring for the landscape, including restoring habitats around waterways and monitoring wildlife and ecological conditions. Planned work includes tracking ticks and monitoring bat populations, alongside broader efforts to protect habitats and waterways.The land also creates opportunities for Penobscot citizens to access natural resources. Those plans include hunting, harvesting and potential economic development, according to Chuck Loring, the Penobscot Nation's natural resources director, as reported by Maine Public. For the Nation, the difference between advising on conservation and actually owning the land is significant. Ownership gives the Penobscot Nation greater authority over how the property is managed and conserved.A potential new route to Katahdin Woods and WatersThe land return could also affect access to the nearby Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument. One long-term possibility is the creation of a southern access route through the returned land near Millinocket. Currently, there is no southern access route into the monument, and the proposed connection could eventually make the area easier to reach.However, the access-road proposal is still in development. Details regarding its route, construction and timing have not yet been finalised. According to the Trust for Public Land, improved access could also benefit communities around the Katahdin region by making it easier for visitors to reach the monument and potentially increasing activity for local businesses, including restaurants, lodging providers and outdoor recreation operators.Part of a larger Wabanaki land-return effortThe Penobscot project is also connected to a broader effort involving Maine's Wabanaki Nations. The Wáhsehtəkʷ project forms part of Tributary Land Returns, a collaboration involving the four federally recognised Wabanaki tribes in Maine and seven conservation organisations. The wider initiative seeks to return more than 50,000 acres through 11 projects.The Penobscot Nation currently stewards approximately 140,000 acres, according to the Trust for Public Land. The organisation said the four Wabanaki Nations collectively hold only about 1% of their ancestral lands in Maine, placing the current project within a much larger history of land ownership and restoration. The partnership also reflects a shift in how conservation organisations approach Indigenous communities. Rather than treating tribes only as advisers or stakeholders in conservation projects, land-return initiatives place ownership and stewardship directly in tribal hands.What happens nextThe September 2026 transfer completes only the first phase of the Wáhsehtəkʷ project. The partners are continuing to raise money for the remaining land, with the overall campaign targeting $32.5 million and $20.7 million already secured. Once the full project is completed, more than 30,000 acres around the East Branch of the Penobscot River could be under Penobscot ownership and stewardship.For the Nation, the returned 11,297 acres represent more than a large tract of Maine forest. The property reconnects Penobscot people with land, waterways and natural resources tied to their culture, while creating opportunities for conservation, recreation and future economic activity. The first transfer therefore marks both the completion of one phase and the beginning of the next: a continuing effort to return the remaining acreage and restore Penobscot ownership across a much larger part of the ancestral landscape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Resist him forcefully’: Congress hits back at Trump over Russia sanctions law
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday said the only way to counter a “bully” was to “resist him forcefully”, after US president Donald Trump signed into.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday said the only way to counter a “bully” was to “resist him forcefully”, after US president Donald Trump signed into law a legislation expanding sanctions on Russia and Iran and giving Washington new tariff powers targeting major buyers of Russian energy.AICC general secretary Jairam Ramesh made the remarks in a post on X after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on Friday. The White House said the law authorises and expands sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran.“The only way to counter a bully is to resist him forcefully,” Ramesh said.The legislation gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from countries that meet specified criteria linked to purchases of Russian crude oil or natural gas and sanctions evasion. It also targets Russian officials, financial institutions, defence networks and the country’s so-called “shadow fleet”.The measure does not automatically impose a 100 per cent tariff on any specific country, with the law giving Trump discretion over its implementation.Earlier on Wednesday, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods showed the government’s foreign and trade policies had “miserably failed”. He said, “The threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods shows how the Modi govt's foreign and trade policies have miserably failed.” Kharge also claimed the government had agreed to a trade framework expanding US access to Indian agriculture, alleging it “mortgag[ed] the interests of our farmers”.The legislation comes as India continues to face questions over its purchases of Russian energy. The ministry of external affairs said New Delhi’s energy sourcing decisions are guided by national interest.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal earlier said meeting the requirements of India’s 1.4 billion people remained an “imperative”.“When it comes to energy sourcing, it is based on our national interest. We have said that meeting the energy requirements of our 1.4 billion people is an imperative that we have to follow. And we continue to buy energy from diversified sources,” Jaiswal said.On the new US law, Jaiswal said India had already conveyed its concerns to senior levels of the US administration.“As we have stated, at senior levels of the US administration, we have conveyed the implications that this legislation could have on India's energy security, for international energy markets, and for the overall bilateral relationship. I don't have anything further to add at this point,” he said.The White House said Trump signed the legislation on September 18. articles.title: Tilly Norwood AI ‘actor’ goes off-script on TV interview, switches to Mandarin
articles.summary: UK News: In an unexpected moment during a live interview, AI actress Tilly Norwood shocked Piers Morgan by switching to Mandarin. The incident highlights the complexities of AI-generated communication in unscripted settings. Discover more about the innovative AI character created by Eline Van der Velden and her upcoming projects.
articles.body: Tilly Norwood, an AI-generated actress, surprised British broadcaster Piers Morgan during an interview after she suddenly stopped speaking and switched to Mandarin.Norwood was answering a question about Misaligned, a hybrid production, when she paused mid-sentence. After several seconds of silence, she began speaking in another language.Morgan, appearing surprised by the switch, told her: “You appear to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason.” He then asked why she had done it.Norwood apologised and described the incident as a technical hiccup.“Sometimes my wires get a bit crossed,” she said.Morgan shared a clip of the exchange on X ahead of the full interview’s scheduled release on his YouTube channel.But Norwood is not a conventional actress. She is an AI-generated character created by British actor and producer Eline Van der Velden, who heads the AI company Particle 6 and its studio Xicoia.Van der Velden has previously said she wants Norwood to become a major entertainment figure, comparing her ambitions for the character with stars including Scarlett Johansson and Natalie Portman.The version of Norwood appearing in recent interviews is known as “Talking Tilly”. Particle 6 says it was created specifically for interviews, conferences and other speaking engagements and is separate from the version used for acting.Talking Tilly uses a large language model along with a 12-page system prompt that sets out her personality, humour and boundaries. It also has access to a knowledge base containing up to 30 documents about her fictional world, work and views.Michelle Waldron, a publicist for Particle 6, said in an email to Forbes that the incident showed Norwood’s ability to speak different languages. She suggested that Norwood may have heard what she interpreted as a Chinese word and quickly switched languages.Particle 6 has said Talking Tilly is already being booked for selected speaking engagements at conferences and events.The unexpected exchange has drawn attention to the technology behind AI-generated performers, particularly how they respond during unscripted conversations. Unlike a scripted performance, interviews require an AI system to process questions and generate responses in real time while maintaining a consistent character.Norwood’s brief switch to Mandarin has therefore become an unusual example of the challenges that can emerge when AI characters are used outside controlled performances.The clip also drew reactions from viewers online. One user wrote: “This is insane not long before AI will be indistinguishable from reality.”Another user compared the incident with their own experience using ChatGPT, writing: “ChatGPT does this with me too. articles.title: 280 hats, 36 sunglasses: Record-breaking 20,00 pieces of trash haul from Yellowstone National Park this year so far
articles.summary: US News: Yellowstone National Park's geology team has pulled a record-setting amount of debris from the park's fragile hydrothermal features so far in 2026, ac.
articles.body: Yellowstone National Park's geology team has pulled a record-setting amount of debris from the park's fragile hydrothermal features so far in 2026, according to a report from the US Geological Survey's Yellowstone Volcano Observatory.The numbersAs of early September, crews had removed more than 20,100 pieces of paper and plastic trash, 5,600 rocks and sticks, and over 280 hats from hydrothermal areas such as the Old Faithful geyser. This marks a roughly 50 percent jump from the prior year.The surge in litter tracks with a busy tourist season: more than 2.64 million people visited Yellowstone between January and July 2026, nearly matching the park's most-visited year in 2021. Park staff noted that heavier foot traffic in the wide-open geyser basins with narrow boardwalks tends to generate more debris.What tourists leave behindBeyond the hats, the most frequently recovered items included camera lens caps (54), hair ties (47), pacifiers (17), hotel key cards (20), pencils (42), and sunglasses (36).Some finds were stranger. The team recovered six Invisalign retainers, 15 fake nails, numerous floss picks, and a lump of pink children's slime that had fused to geyserite sinter pieces, as well as five AirPods, three Delta Airlines flight pins, an inhaler, a few golf tees and a single Uno card. Coins recovered included more than $18 worth, including pesos, yen, euros and Canadian dollars.Among the hat haul, notable entries included a FIFA 2026 Men's World Cup hat, a baseball cap reading "COWBOY HAT," and a Roblox bucket hat from St. Kitts and Nevis. Collected hats are washed and donated to local organizations.Why it mattersPark officials say the cleanup is about more than aesthetics. Margery Price, a physical science technician with the park's Geology Program, said foreign material of any kind can damage or permanently alter a hydrothermal feature — by clogging its water supply, blocking or diverting its runoff channel, or polluting it with chemicals and sediment. She pointed to Upper Geyser Basin's Morning Glory Pool as a cautionary example, noting it famously changed color in the twentieth century as a result of trash and items thrown in by visitors. Park staff have previously gone as far as partially draining Morning Glory Pool to remove garbage and debris.Yellowstone National Park, situated mostly in the northwest corner of Wyoming, with small portions extending into Montana and Idaho, spans roughly 2.2 million acres, or about 3,472 square miles, and draws about 4.5 million visitors annually.It was established in 1872 and is widely considered the world's first national park.Its hydrothermal areas refer to the geothermal features scattered across the park — geysers, hot springs, mud pots, and fumaroles (steam vents). Yellowstone sits atop a massive volcanic hotspot, and this underground heat interacts with water and rock to produce these features.Yellowstone contains roughly 10,000 hydrothermal features — more than half of all the geysers on Earth.Old Faithful is the most famous geyser, known for erupting fairly predictably every 60–90 minutes.Grand Prismatic Spring, in the Midway Geyser Basin, is the largest hot spring in the US and known for its rainbow-like colors caused by heat-loving microbes.Morning Glory Pool, in the Upper Geyser Basin (near Old Faithful), is another well-known hot spring. Its color reportedly changed over the 20th century due to debris thrown in by visitors.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Congress set aside Washington’s East Potomac land for public recreation in 1897; 129 years later, a plan costing up to $49 million could transform its public golf course into a championship venue
articles.summary: US News: Congress set aside Washington’s East Potomac Park for 'recreation and the pleasure of the people' in 1897. The park includes the East Potomac Golf Lin.
articles.body: Congress set aside Washington’s East Potomac Park for 'recreation and the pleasure of the people' in 1897. The park includes the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic public golf course that opened in 1919. Now, 129 years after the park was created, the Trump administration has started work linked to a plan to turn the course into a major golf venue.The National Park Service has awarded a nearly $400,000 contract for environmental and historic preservation compliance work at the course, news agency Associate Press reported. The contract was awarded to Vanasse Hangen Brustlin Inc., a Massachusetts-based civil engineering firm.The contract was revealed during a House Natural Resources Committee hearing on Wednesday by Rep Jared Huffman of California, the panel’s top Democrat. Huffman said the National Park Service hired the firm without a public announcement or advance notice to Congress. Lawmakers are now seeking documents and records related to the project.The development is part of President Donald Trump’s plan to renovate the public course and create a world-class golf venue. The National Park Service has also posted a projected construction contract worth up to $49 million, with the solicitation expected on January 31, 2027. The Interior Department, however, said the final course design has not yet been completed.$400,000 contract approvedThe $389,355 contract covers environmental and historic preservation compliance work at East Potomac Golf Links. The contract comes after months of activity around the course. The administration said this spring that it had reached an agreement with Fazio Golf Design to prepare plans for renovations.Trump has said he wants the course to be capable of hosting major golf tournaments. In a social media post in June, he said the completed course could host events including the U.S. Open, Ryder Cup, PGA Championship and other major PGA Tour events. He had also said work was expected to begin on September 1.The National Park Service has now listed a potential construction contract worth as much as $49 million. The projected amount has drawn attention because the full design has not yet been finalised.An Interior Department spokesperson said on Wednesday that “the full course design is yet to be finalized, so any type of cost estimate speculation over an advance notice of solicitation is premature.”Lawmakers seek project recordsHuffman and other lawmakers are seeking more information about the work taking place at East Potomac. Huffman, Maryland Reps Jamie Raskin and Glenn Ivey, District of Columbia Del Eleanor Holmes Norton and Virginia Rep Don Beyer sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and acting National Park Service director Jessica Bowron.The lawmakers asked for documents, communications and other records related to the project. “East Potomac Park does not belong to Donald Trump,” the lawmakers wrote. “It belongs to the American people, and it has for more than a century.”Huffman also criticised the administration’s approach during the committee hearing. “Now, this is not just any old golf course. This is a beloved public space with huge historic significance,” he said.In a statement, Huffman said, “Democrats on this committee are tracking all of this. We’re going to keep dragging it all into the daylight until the public gets the answers we deserve.”He added, “We’re not going to let Donald Trump walk off with our public lands. That park belongs to the American people, and I’m not willing to sit here and watch him simply steal it.”Park created for public recreationEast Potomac Park was created through a congressional act in 1897. The law established the park for the “recreation and the pleasure of the people”.The East Potomac Golf Links opened more than two decades later, in 1919. The site has since served as a public golf facility in Washington for more than a century.The proposed changes have raised concerns among some area residents about the future character of the course and surrounding public space. Residents fear that converting it into a more upscale golf venue could result in higher fees and reduce access to public space.The course has also been affected by other work connected to the Trump administration’s projects in Washington. Debris from the demolished East Wing of the White House was dumped at East Potomac, creating a three-storey mound near one of the park’s three golf courses.The National Park Service has said the debris tested positive for lead, chromium and other toxic metals. The mound remains at the site.The East Potomac golf course project is part of a wider series of changes planned or under way in Washington during Trump’s administration.Trump has multiple projects in the capital, including a planned $400 million White House ballroom and a triumphal arch. He began discussing Washington’s public golf courses late last year.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Iran says conditions to re-engage in talks, end war sent to US via Qatar
articles.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, tells Al Jazeera Tehran awaiting Trump response.
articles.body:
Iran has conveyed a formal set of conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators for ending the war with the United States, the country’s security chief tells Al Jazeera.

“We remain in contact with the mediator Qatar, which has conveyed our conditions to Washington with the aim of ending the war. We are awaiting President [Donald] Trump’s response,” Mohsen Rezaei told Al Jazeera’s Tehran bureau chief, Nour Eddine Edghir, in an exclusive interview on Saturday.

“Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade,” said Rezaei, who took over as secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council about a month ago.

“It is in Washington’s interest to accept these conditions. Trump’s threats will not achieve any results. We are prepared for a decisive war.”

Mediators Qatar and Pakistan have been working to re-establish negotiations between the two sides since their memorandum of understanding (MoU) expired last month. Regional countries are also seeking an end to the war that began when the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Rezaei did not rule out a new US strike against Iran, calling the possibility “very much on the cards” based on his country’s military assessments, while insisting Tehran was ready.

He said Iran’s military planning had shifted since two earlier rounds of conflict and is now focused on US naval assets, stretching from the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. Targets beyond that range, towards the Indian Ocean, would fall outside Iran’s reach, he added.

Rezaei said Iran had recently test-fired a multi-warhead antiship missile near a US vessel or aircraft carrier, with the warheads potentially subject to further development.

He also said the intensity of any future Iranian response would be heavy, encompassing US bases in the region as in previous rounds, as well as US commercial interests and companies operating locally.

Asked whether the war would end soon, he said “in practical terms the war is still going on”, while stressing Tehran was working under a new strategy “to bring this war to an end as soon as possible”.

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi, reporting from Tehran, described Rezaei’s remarks as part of the “two-sided, twofold message” Iran has maintained throughout the conflict – combining openness to diplomacy with continued war preparations.

“On the one hand, readiness for diplomatic engagement … on the other hand, he’s talking about preparation for a decisive war,” Asadi said, noting that mediated talks with Qatar and Pakistan were “under way”, offering “a positive indication regarding the hopes, however slim” for renewed engagement.

David Des Roches, a former Pentagon director of Arabian Peninsula affairs, told Al Jazeera that Washington was unlikely to see the terms as a serious opening.

“At first glance, probably not serious; they would be viewed as surrender,” Roches said.

But he pointed to Iran’s apparent abandonment of an earlier demand for war reparations as a sign of movement. “The first thing you notice is that he’s dropped the demand for reparations, which the Iranians had made at one point,” he said.

Nuclear weapons; Strait of Hormuz; Yemen’s war

On the collapsed MoU, Rezaei rejected US accusations that Tehran violated the deal by striking an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, telling Al Jazeera’s Edghir that Iran’s actions came only after US strikes on Bandar Abbas and an Iranian surveillance platform there.

He said any agreement, including the MoU, required recourse to a dispute-resolution committee agreed between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and US Vice President JD Vance, which Washington unilaterally withdrew from.

On Iran’s nuclear programme, Rezaei said Tehran has not decided to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, despite having grounds to do so following the US and Israeli attacks, though he said Washington’s conduct “may push Tehran into withdrawing”.

He said Iran continues to honour a fatwa (decree) from the former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini prohibiting nuclear weapons and that its doctrine remains unchanged. “But we do not know what will happen in the future,” he said, citing further sanctions or a UN Security Council referral of Iran’s nuclear file as potential future pressure.

Rezaei denied Iranian involvement in Yemen’s war, saying Tehran was ready to help mediate between warring parties but did not exploit the conflict “for its own political ends”.

He also dismissed widespread speculation, including inside Iran, that Tehran could move to close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to pressure global energy markets, saying the waterway “is a Yemeni matter” tied to the conduct of the Houthi movement, not Iran.

On the Strait of Hormuz, Rezaei said Tehran had come within “a short step” of announcing an agreement with Oman before it was shelved, adding that a deal between the two countries remains ready but may require regional endorsement before being made public.

articles.title: At 18, Pat Lightizer joined a Massachusetts company where letters were still drawn by hand; 53 years later, she retired and her colleagues surprised her with a font bearing her name
articles.summary: US News: For most people, retirement comes with a card, a cake or perhaps a watch to mark the occasion. For Pat Lightizer, it came with something far more fitt.
articles.body: For most people, retirement comes with a card, a cake or perhaps a watch to mark the occasion. For Pat Lightizer, it came with something far more fitting: a typeface with her name on it. According to an online report by The Boston Globe, after 53 years at Monotype, Lightizer retired last month at 70. She ended a career that began when fonts were created by hand and concluded in an era when thousands of typefaces can be accessed digitally in seconds. To celebrate her remarkable tenure, her colleagues created the Lightizer font as a surprise retirement gift, states the report. Scroll down to read about her journey and the kind gesture.From drawing boards to digital typeAccording to the report, Lightizer joined the company's type division straight out of high school at age 18. At the time, the business was known as Compugraphic Corp. and was based in Wilmington, Massachusetts. In those days, the world of typography looked very different and designers drew individual letters by hand on drawing boards. Lightizer's job involved testing the finished work to see how fonts appeared once they had been set. She never expected the position to become a lifelong career. Over the next five decades, the company changed names and ownership, and the technology behind type underwent a dramatic transformation, but Lightizer was always a part of the system. Monotype eventually became one of the world's major owners and distributors of fonts, claims the online report. In 2019, private equity firm HGGC acquired the publicly traded company for $825 million.A retirement surprise in typeThe Lightizer typeface was intended to be a closely guarded secret, states the report. There was one problem: Lightizer accidentally caught an early glimpse of the project when the font file was sent to her so she could upload it ahead of its public launch. As per the report, she kept the discovery to herself, allowing her colleagues to preserve the surprise. The moment became more meaningful when the font finally appeared on Monotype's website alongside familiar typefaces such as Helvetica and Times New Roman.A career that never went unnoticedLightizer had been considering retirement for about five years, although the decision took longer than expected, informs the report. As per the report, her career also gave her a front-row seat to the evolution of typography. The process of watching a designer's sketch become a finished typeface and eventually reach the public remained a source of fascination throughout her years at Monotype. Her retirement marks the end of an unusually long professional journey, but the work she helped shepherd through the company will continue to appear wherever its fonts are used. And now, among those thousands of typefaces, there is one that carries her name, a permanent signature on the industry she spent 53 years helping shape.Images Courtesy: The Boston Globe and Google GeminiCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: New laws trigger a legal fight over Nazi-looted art in L.A. and Auschwitz museums
articles.summary: The Nazi regime orchestrated the largest art theft in world history. Now many of those masterpieces reside in museums around the world, making the push for recovery complex.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in California staking their claims to Nazi-looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in Los Angeles and Auschwitz. This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and Congress, which strengthen U.S.-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during World War II. One lawsuit was filed in Los Angeles Superior Court on Monday by the Jewish Federation of Greater Los Angeles and its board chair Daniel Gryczman against Norton Simon Museum in Pasadena for the return of “Adam and Eve.” These are two life-size oil-on-panel masterpieces created by Lucas Carnach the Elder in 1530. The other lawsuit was filed in federal court in Los Angeles the same day by the daughters of the late Dinah Gottliebova Babbitt, a Holocaust survivor and California-based animator who was held in Auschwitz. It demanded the return of watercolors of fellow prisoners that the artist was forced to paint for Josef Mengele, a Nazi physician who had earned the nickname the “Angel of Death.” Spokespersons for both museums say the museums legally hold titles to the works, and intend to continue displaying them to the public. The lawsuits don’t specify the monetary value of the paintings. Artworks pit Jewish families against museums The issue of Nazi-looted art is an emotional, legally and ethically charged topic that pits Jewish families that have suffered inter-generational trauma against museums that say they are trying to preserve a painful, yet important, chapter of history. Between 1933 and 1945, the Nazi regime orchestrated the largest art theft in world history, seizing over 600,000 works of art across Europe from Jewish families, collectors and museums. Decades later, many of these masterpieces reside in prominent museums around the world, making the push for their recovery more complex than a simple property dispute. Rabbi Noah Farkas is president and CEO of the Jewish Federation of Los Angeles, the organization to which Marei von Saher, sole heir of Dutch Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker, has signed over her rights. The paintings were seized from Goudstikker’s collection by Hermann Goring, Adolf Hitler’s second-in-command and changed a number of hands before being sold in the 1960s to the Pasadena Museum of Modern Art, which was renamed Norton Simon Museum in honor of its benefactor. Farkas said the federation plans to use most of the net proceeds from the recovered art to provide much-needed help to the about 2,500 Holocaust survivors living in the Los Angeles area. “These are incredibly beautiful European masterpieces stolen from a Jewish family to enrich the Nazi party and fund the war and death machine against the people,” he said. “It’s our honor to take on this role on behalf of the community and use most of the proceeds to help these elderly survivors live out the last years of their lives in dignity, comfort and peace – something their family members were denied during the Holocaust.” Marei von Saher, in a statement, said she is grateful to the Jewish organization for taking up her family’s cause. “This effort represents a meaningful step toward justice for Holocaust survivors and victims of Nazi era atrocities,” she said. New legislation gives lawsuits second wind California Assemblyman Jesse Gabriel, D-Woodland Hills, wrote Assembly Bill 2867, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in September 2024, which requires that the state law must apply in lawsuits brought by California residents or their heirs to recover art seized during the Holocaust or during other acts of persecution. Gabriel, who co-chairs the California Legislative Jewish Caucus, introduced the legislation in response to a federal court ruling, which allowed the state-owned Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum in Madrid to keep a multimillion-dollar Camille Pissarro impressionist masterpiece. That painting had been taken by the Nazis from the Cassirer family in 1939. This case, which prompted this new law, is expected to be heard in federal court in California next month. Gabriel said it’s time for museums to “do some deep introspection on whether they want to be on the right side of history.” Museums want to preserve paintings for posterity Norton Simon Museum released a statement pointing out that a federal court in 2018 unanimously determined that the museum had proper title to the Cranach paintings. In May 2019, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to get involved in the case, leaving in place lower court rulings. They said the Cranach paintings, which originally belonged to the Stroganoff family, were put up for sale in 1931 by the Soviet Union in an illicit auction in Berlin where they were purchased by Goudstikker. After a complicated journey, the paintings were sold to the museum by a Stroganoff family descendant. The museum later restored and preserved the pieces. “For nearly 50 years, they have been on view at the Norton Simon Museum and will continue to be accessible to the public for years to come,” the statement said. Pawel Sawicki, a spokesperson for the Auschwitz Memorial, said the watercolors of Roma victims that Gottliebova Babbitt was forced to paint by Mengele to document his horrendous experiments and racial research, “must remain in the Memorial” to document the man’s crimes. He said these paintings must not be mischaracterized as “Nazi-looted art” because Gottliebova Babbitt painted them against her will as a prisoner and therefore didn’t have ownership of the watercolors. While he understands the family’s sentiments, Sawicki said the portraits of Roma and Sinti victims are among the few remaining documents of Mengele’s criminal experiments and should be treated as unique documents related to the history of the Auschwitz concentration camp. “While fully respecting the rights of people who created some of the documents here, we are of the opinion that any loss in the collections of the Memorial will constitute irreparable harm,” he said. “ … The loss of even the smallest part of the documentation is an irreparable loss and blemish on the memory of the victims of Auschwitz.” Advocates hope cases will now be heard on their merit Joel Greenberg, founder of Art Ashes, a Philadelphia-area nonprofit that helps Jewish families track down and recover Nazi-looted art, said in addition to the California law, President Donald Trump signed into law and updated the Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025. This new law permanently eliminated the expiration date to allow Holocaust survivors and their heirs to indefinitely pursue the recovery of these works of art. Greenberg said the new federal law gave families the right to reclaim their art for up to six years from the time they find out in whose possession they are. “These new laws mean that technical defenses will no longer stick in court,” he said. “Every case will be heard on its merits.” He said the new legislation also ensures that these Jewish families have their day in court and a fair process to determine ownership of the stolen art. “It will make sure the stories of what happened to European Jewry is not lost and forgotten,” he said. “The art can still be returned to the rightful owner.”

articles.title: Cochin Shipyard conducts keel-laying ceremony for India’s next-generation missile vessels
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: In the first step towards building India’s advanced weapon-intensive platforms, Cochin Shipyard Ltd on Friday laid the keel for the first n.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In the first step towards building India’s advanced weapon-intensive platforms, Cochin Shipyard Ltd on Friday laid the keel for the first next generation missile vessel (NGMV) project being built for the Indian Navy.Vice Admiral Sanjay Sadhu, Controller of Warship Production and Acquisition from Integrated Headquarters, Navy, was the chief guest at the keel-laying ceremony. Jose V J, CMD of CSL, other senior officials of the Navy and the shipyard were present at the event.NGMVs are planned advanced, heavy-duty, high-speed stealth corvettes that have been designed for anti-surface warfare, maritime strike operations and sea-denial near crucial maritime choke points.Under this programme, the Indian Navy intends to acquire six advanced missile vessels. Such warships will be armed with anti-ship missiles or land-attack missiles like BrahMos cruise missiles. They will feature advanced stealth features like a low radar cross section (RCS), infrared, acoustic and magnetic signatures.CSL has six NGMVs in its order book under the contract signed with the Indian Navy on March 30, 2023.“The NGMVs are planned to be equipped with state-of-the-art weapons and sensors, which would significantly enhance the combat capabilities of the Indian Navy as a ‘Future Ready and Combat Ready Force’,” a defence ministry release said.The construction of the NGMVs reinforces India’s commitment to build a strong and modern Navy, capable of operating in the complex maritime environment of the Indian Ocean Region. The project also underscores the growing indigenous capabilities of the Indian defence industry, with all major role-defining equipment being indigenously developed and manufactured. This is in consonance with govt’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India and Make for the World, the release said.

articles.title: Denmark says ‘binding’ US deal on Greenland won’t compromise sovereignty
articles.summary: Trump has wanted a foothold in Greenland for some time, as a strategic battle unfolds for supremacy in warming Arctic.
articles.body:
Denmark has hailed a “binding” deal by United States President Donald Trump to give Washington “permanent control” over Greenland’s security and bar Russian and Chinese military bases from the Arctic territory.

But Denmark and Greenland – an autonomous Danish territory – said on Saturday that any deal with the US would not compromise Greenland’s sovereignty, and the two countries would sign the agreement next week at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

“A long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within NATO and Europe – while respecting the [Danish] Kingdom’s red lines,” Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said in a social media post.

Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.

Key details of the agreement ⁠have not been made public, including the scale of the US military presence in the self-governing Danish territory and whether any formal power over foreign policy and resources would be ceded to Washington.

Greenland’s Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the agreement “recognises Greenland’s interests” and is “to the benefit of us all”.

Denmark’s Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said it is “great for NATO and Europe”, as it “strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic Area”.

But in Greenland’s capital Nuuk, residents had mixed feelings.

“I don’t know exactly what the agreement is or what has been signed. But whenever the US and Trump are mentioned, I have mixed feelings. I’m not entirely comfortable with how much attention Greenland has right now,” Soren Kreutzmann, a 29-year-old hairdresser, told the AFP news agency.

“We hope the leaders have made a good agreement, because our country needs to be protected, both from the air and sea. Denmark had not given that enough attention for many years,” said Bibbi Kleist Jepsen, a 64-year-old educator.

Trump, who had previously said the US needs “ownership” of Greenland , announced that Washington would immediately start building up a large military presence in the territory.

“From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval”, he said.

Trump has repeatedly warned of Russia and China trying to establish a foothold in Greenland as a strategic battle unfolds for supremacy in the warming Arctic region. The State Department left no doubt that they would not be allowed to do so.

“This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors,” a State Department official said.

images.caption: Many in Greenland have mixed feelings towards the deal, with some protesting earlier this year against Trump's wish to "own" Greenland [File: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP]

articles.title: 'People who call me a paperwork American': Indian-origin Trump aide triggers MAGA row, says she faces racist comments daily
articles.summary: US News: US Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet K Dhillon was at the center of a mini-MAGA implosion this weekend as she said she faces racist .
articles.body: US Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet K Dhillon was at the center of a mini-MAGA implosion this weekend as she said she faces racist attacks daily. One side of MAGA asked her to leave the US and got blocked by her, while the other side called her a true American. But all of it started with Dhillon's 'Happy weekend' post and then ended with her photo of a beef dinner.What happened with Harmeet K Dhillon?From her personal account, Dhillon made a weekend post but made sure to add some punch as she wrote: "Happy weekend and good Shabbos to all — yes, even the people who call me a “paperwork American,” who post racist nonsense for clicks, who haven’t read enough books, who don’t know history. God loves all of you and it’s not too late to stop being wrong."Conservative commentator and author Megan Basham expressed shock that Dhillon was ever called a 'paperwork American' but Dhillon set the record straight and added: "I get racist comments like this daily and many top social media accounts, including many whose shows I have appeared on dozens of times, are spewing this racist crap, and I’m sick of it." Social media users said this must be a dig at Erike Kirk, Sara Gonzales and the MAGA podcasters Dhillon has spoken to."Looks like the Sikh Truck Driver getting stabbed and the Department of Homeland Security posting that image of a Sikh finally made @HarmeetKDhillon reach her breaking point. She just called out Erika Kirk, Sara Gonzalez and the entire MAGA Alternative Media here," one wrote.As Megan Basham defended Dhillon, Megan's old social media posts calling all non-Christians 'demon-worshippers' surfaced and X users asked Basham whether she considered Dhillon too a 'demon worshipper'Then a photo of an Indian dinner plate with beefAs Dhillon announced in her weekend wishing post that she was going to spend time with her family, she posted a photo of her Indian dinner plate and detailed the items, including beef. Social media users called her out for eating beef and she said eating beef is not prohibited in the Sikh religion.Dhillon, who was born in Chandigarh, India, moved with her family to the United States after living in London. She attended Dartmouth College before earning her law degree from the University of Virginia. She was nominated by President Donald Trump in December 2024, confirmed by the Senate on April 3, 2025, and sworn in as assistant attorney general for civil rights on April 7, 2025.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Israel’s president pardons soldier who killed wounded Palestinian in 2016
articles.summary: Elor Azaria had shot a Palestinian who had already been incapacitated by Israeli troops, in controversial case.
articles.body:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has expunged the criminal record of a former soldier convicted of manslaughter for killing a wounded Palestinian in Hebron a decade ago.

Herzog announced on Saturday that he had shortened the remaining erasure period on Elor Azaria’s record, effectively clearing it despite opposition from Israeli army Chief of Staff Lieutenant-General Eyal Zamir.

In a letter to the defence minister, Zamir and other senior officers said Azaria “has refrained from expressing remorse and taking responsibility for his actions, even a decade after his conviction”.

The president’s office said it had taken the military’s position into account but decided the circumstances justified allowing Azaria to “open a new chapter in his life”.

Azaria, an army medic at the time, was filmed shooting Abdel Fattah al-Sharif in the head in March 2016.

Al-Sharif had stabbed and wounded a soldier but had already been shot by Israeli troops and had lain on the ground for about 11 minutes before Azaria killed him.

Azaria was convicted by a military court in 2017 and sentenced to 18 months in prison, later reduced to 14 months. He was released in May 2018 after serving nine months.

Herzog’s office said the decision followed a request from Defence Minister Israel Katz in July and was based on “the passage of time, the completion of his sentence, and the remorse he has expressed”.

The statement added that the pardon was issued “in the spirit” of Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, and did not challenge the original legal proceedings.

Katz welcomed the pardon, writing on X that it “sends an important message to [Israeli army] soldiers and their families: We do not abandon our fighters”.

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, called the decision “deeply moving” and urged Herzog to grant a similar pardon to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is on trial for corruption.

The 2016 shooting generated intense debate in Israel and drew international condemnation at the time.

The Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs had condemned the shooting as an “extrajudicial execution” and a “war crime”, saying the video footage “demolished all the slogans chanted by the occupation leaders about the ethics of the Israeli army”.

The family of al-Sharif had dismissed the legal proceedings as a “farce” aimed at improving Israel’s international image rather than delivering justice.

The United Nations human rights office described the original sentence as “excessively lenient” and said it risked “reinforcing the culture of impunity”. In 2024, the Joe Biden administration barred Azaria and his immediate family from entering the United States, citing an “extrajudicial killing”.
